attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: No current constructive Yang-Mills estimate proves that reflected Wilson collar products have zero connected coincident-footprint boundary OPE after one-body perimeter/area/cusp renormalization. The gap is especially sharp for hairpin or cusp degenerations at t=0, where a pair-dependent anomalous dimension could produce K!=0.
steps: Fix a finite family of positive-time Wilson collar observables. For every delta>0, regulated reflection positivity and the fixed-collar RG-to-OS passage give a positive finite matrix N^{(delta)}; if every reflected entry converges, closedness of the positive cone gives N=lim_{delta downarrow 0}N^{(delta)}>=0.

Insert the most general finite boundary trace expansion compatible with multiplicative Wilson renormalization plus additive contacts: N=Gamma circ M + A. Here M is the intended same-theory OS matrix; Gamma records pair-dependent boundary factors not already absorbed into one-body normalizations.

Use diagonal trace continuity: A_{ii}=0 after the locked one-body normalization. If A is a positive additive contact kernel, Cauchy-Schwarz gives |A_{ij}|^2<=A_{ii}A_{jj}=0, so A=0. Thus a genuine positive additive boundary defect cannot survive once the diagonal trace is valid.

With A=0, the intended matrix is M=Gamma^{[-1]} circ N. Schur product theory says positivity is preserved for all possible positive N if Gamma^{[-1]} is positive semidefinite. If Gamma is also a positive boundary kernel with normalized diagonal, then positivity of both Gamma and Gamma^{[-1]} forces |Gamma_{ij}|=1 in every 2-by-2 minor, hence Gamma_{ij}=alpha_i overline{alpha_j}; this is exactly K=0.

Therefore the substantive Yang-Mills estimate is not the formal closed-cone passage but the assertion that the connected coincident-footprint boundary OPE has no multiplicative cross-ratio contribution for the locked Wilson algebra.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: The finite-dimensional Schur/cross-ratio argument is valid, but it is conditional on an analytic boundary OPE and on positivity/vanishing properties of additive contacts. The missing theorem is a same-theory trace theorem for mixed Wilson products, not another abstract topology.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Reflection-Positivity Closed-Cone Topology: Wilson Boundary Cross-Ratio Test

assumptions: For each fixed collar distance delta>0, RG convergence controls all finite reflected OS matrix entries for A_+^{lock}.
Diagonal trace continuity is valid: each individual Wilson collar has the intended boundary limit after the predeclared one-body renormalization.

Mixed reflected Wilson collar limits admit a finite boundary expansion N_{ij}=Gamma_{ij} M_{ij}+A_{ij}, where N is the collar-limit OS matrix, M is the intended target OS matrix, Gamma_{ij}!=0 is multiplicative, and A is additive contact.
The additive contact part, when present as an independent boundary OPE contribution to a positive collar theory, is positive semidefinite as a finite OS kernel.
definitions: source object: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms S_{a,L} on a locked gauge-invariant positive-time algebra A_+^{lock}, with Wilson-loop collar observables W(C_\delta) and mirror-flat local composites, converging on fixed-collar reflected probes.

target object: continuum Schwinger functions S on the same locked algebra, satisfying OS positivity so that OS reconstruction yields a Hilbert space, vacuum vector, and positive time-translation generator.

controlled interface: regulated reflection-positive Schwinger forms -> OS-positive continuum Schwinger functions, with the only delicate interface being the trace limit from positive-time collars to observables touching the reflection plane.

same-theory condition: the cutoff embeddings and collar maps identify the same gauge-invariant observable before and after cutoff removal; one-body Wilson renormalizations are allowed as fixed diagonal congruences, but any pair-dependent boundary factor or boundary counterterm is a falsifier unless it has zero logarithmic cross-ratio.

equations.label: fixed-collar OS matrix
equations.valid_when: The collar supports stay in t>0 at distance delta from the reflection plane and the regulated reflection positivity plus RG convergence are valid for these reflected probes.

equations.label: boundary anomaly decomposition
equations.valid_when: The Wilson collar trace has a finite boundary OPE expansion after fixed one-body renormalizations; M is the intended same-theory matrix entry.

equations.label: logarithmic cross-ratio obstruction
equations.valid_when: All Gamma entries are nonzero and a consistent branch of log Gamma is chosen on the finite family; K=0 for all i,k,j,ell exactly means Gamma_{ij}=alpha_i\overline{alpha_j} on each connected component.

equations.label: Schur transfer criterion
equations.valid_when: The boundary anomaly decomposition is valid entrywise; positivity transfers from every positive N to M if A=0 and Gamma^{[-1]} is a positive Schur multiplier, with the same-theory case reducing to K=0 under positivity of Gamma.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: Find four Wilson collar observables with coincident boundary footprint for which K_{ik;jl} is nonzero, or find an additive contact A with zero diagonal that cannot be forced to vanish by positivity; either is a concrete falsifier of the same-theory OS bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the vague Wilson boundary-renormalization problem into a finite-dimensional invariant-preservation theorem: the closed OS cone already gives N>=0, so the only remaining same-theory obstruction is the connected multiplicative boundary anomaly measured by K.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Finite OS-matrix same-theory transfer across the reflection plane is valid for Wilson-loop collars if and only if every boundary multiplicative anomaly is either absent or a rank-one diagonal congruence already included in the locked observable normalization; equivalently the logarithmic anomaly cross-ratio K vanishes on every finite reflected Wilson family. Any nonzero connected coincident-footprint boundary OPE coefficient gives a same-theory falsifier.

assumptions: A small-loop/short-distance OPE for Wilson collars exists uniformly in the cutoff-removal limit.
One-body perimeter, area, and cusp renormalizations have already been locked into the observable definition.
The remaining connected boundary term is bilinear to second order in infinitesimal loop-shape variations.
definitions: Wilson hairpin collar: a pair of short Wilson arcs in t>0 whose reflected product approaches a cusp or hairpin at t=0 as delta downarrow 0.
Boundary current of a small loop: the first nontrivial shape derivative J_C of log W(C_delta) localized on the limiting boundary footprint.
Connected boundary kernel: the coefficient B(J_C,J_D) in the multiplicative anomaly b(C,D) after subtracting one-body terms.
Polarized cross-ratio: K(C_1,C_2;D_1,D_2)=B(J_{C_1}-J_{C_2},J_{D_1}-J_{D_2}) to leading order in the small-loop deformation.

equations.label: hairpin anomaly polarization
equations.valid_when: The Wilson-loop boundary OPE is expanded near a reference mirror-smooth collar and all one-body terms are subtracted.

equations.label: local K probe
equations.valid_when: The four loops are small deformations of the same boundary footprint, so the same branch of the logarithmic anomaly applies.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: A perturbative or constructive estimate giving B(J,J')!=0 for some boundary currents immediately yields nonzero K and hence a falsifier for the same-theory bridge.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Supplies a computable obstruction: rather than trying to prove all Wilson trace continuity at once, test whether the connected boundary OPE kernel vanishes by varying small reflected hairpins.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Infinitesimal reflected hairpin Wilson loops provide a local falsifier probe for K: if the boundary OPE contains a nonzero connected bilinear kernel between the two reflected boundary footprints, then small loop variations polarize that kernel and produce a nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot if a model calculation or known Wilson-loop renormalization theorem gives nonzero connected hairpin K, or if RG compactness cannot control mixed reflected Wilson probes.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote if one proves K=0 for a dense mirror-smooth Wilson core and proves fixed-collar RG convergence dominates the corresponding finite reflected OS matrices.
control_decision.reason: The branch has reduced the broad reflection-positivity passage to a concrete Wilson boundary invariant with a finite-dimensional valid transfer theorem and an explicit local falsifier probe.

dependency_updates.description: The formal fixed-collar closed-cone passage is settled; the lemma now depends on proving K=0 for mixed reflected Wilson boundary traces or restricting to a dense core where Wilson K is absent.
The algebra must record which one-body Wilson renormalizations are built in before taking the collar trace. Pair-dependent boundary factors cannot be silently absorbed without changing the theory.
The topology must control finite OS matrices of mixed reflected Wilson collars, not merely single-loop expectations or local composites away from t=0.

falsifiers: Nonzero logarithmic cross-ratio K_{ik;jl} computed for four reflected Wilson hairpin collars with the same boundary footprint.
A pair-dependent multiplicative damping Gamma_{ij} with normalized |Gamma_{ij}|<1 for some mixed Wilson entry; the reciprocal multiplier then fails the 2-by-2 positivity test.
Failure of RG convergence for mixed reflected Wilson products even though single Wilson-loop collars converge; this would show the cutoff-removal topology is not valid for OS probes.
A boundary counterterm required only for reflected products, not for individual Wilson observables; this changes the test algebra and is a same-theory falsifier.
An additive contact matrix with zero diagonal but nonzero off-diagonal contribution, contradicting positive contact compatibility and indicating an uncontrolled indefinite boundary OPE term.
branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 189 identifies the next invariant more locally: K is not just an abstract finite-matrix obstruction but the polarization of a connected boundary OPE kernel for reflected Wilson hairpins. The valid linear-algebra bridge says positivity survives the collar limit only through zero/rank-one multiplicative anomaly after additive contacts vanish. Thus the analytic Yang-Mills target is precise: prove the connected coincident-footprint boundary kernel is zero on the locked Wilson core, or compute a nonzero hairpin K as a falsifier.
branch_outputs.next_experiment: Work out the infinitesimal hairpin expansion in a controlled model or perturbative Yang-Mills gauge-invariant regularization: isolate one-body cusp/perimeter terms, compute the connected boundary bilinear B(J,J'), and test whether its polarized cross-ratio K vanishes.
